Build the call tree of every function defined in a directory of R files

call_tree_dir.Rd

call_tree_dir() parses every .R file in path without evaluating any of it, extracts each top-level function definition (name <- function(...) ...), and builds the call graph among those locally-defined functions. The result is the tree of calls reachable from root, in the same shape call_stack() returns, so it prints the same way.

Unlike call_stack(), which resolves an already-loaded function through R's own namespace lookup, call_tree_dir() never loads or runs the scanned files. That makes it usable on a package's R/ directory, or a Shiny app's source, without installing or sourcing it first.

Usage

call_tree_dir(
  path = "R",
  root,
  modules_only = FALSE,
  exclude = NULL,
  max_depth = Inf,
  keep = NULL,
  prune = NULL,
  include_ns = NULL,
  include_defaults = FALSE
)

Arguments

path

Character scalar; directory containing .R files. Default "R".

root

Character scalar; name of the function to root the tree at. Must be one of the top-level functions found in path; otherwise call_tree_dir() errors rather than returning an empty tree.

modules_only

Logical. When TRUE, prune the tree to root, the functions root calls directly, and functions that call shiny::NS() or shiny::moduleServer() (Shiny modules); everything else is spliced out, promoting its children so modules reached through a non-module wrapper function stay visible. Default FALSE, which keeps every locally-defined function reachable from root.

exclude

Character vector of function names to drop from the tree, e.g. a logging helper such as "logr_msg" that appears under every node. A dropped function's children are spliced up into its place, as with modules_only. The root is never dropped. Default NULL, which drops nothing.

max_depth

Number of levels to show below root. Default Inf, which shows the whole tree; 1 shows only the functions root calls. Counted after modules_only, exclude, prune, and keep are applied.

keep

Character vector of regular expressions, e.g. "^mod_counts_". When given, the tree is trimmed to nodes whose name matches one of them (with their full subtrees) plus the nodes on the path from root down to each match. Use "^name$" for an exact name. Default NULL, which keeps everything.

prune

Character vector of function names to drop together with everything below them. Unlike exclude, children are not spliced up. Default NULL, which drops nothing.

include_ns

Character vector of package names, e.g. c("shiny", "bslib"). Calls to functions exported by these packages (bare, as pkg::fun(), or pkg:::fun()) are shown as nodes, nested by how the calls are written: shinyApp(ui = app_ui, server = app_server) puts app_ui and app_server under shinyApp. External functions are not followed into their own source, and syntax such as braces, <-, or if is never shown (so "base" is usable). The packages must be installed. Default NULL, which shows only locally-defined functions.

include_defaults

Logical. When TRUE, calls in default argument values (function(dir = util_dir())) are included alongside calls in the body. Default FALSE.

Value

An object of class call_stack (see call_stack()).

Details

When modules_only = TRUE, the functions root calls directly (such as app_ui() and app_server()) are always kept, so UI and server modules stay grouped under them.

A function defined more than once in path raises a warning naming the files; the definition parsed last (files in alphabetical order) is used.

See also

call_tree_app() for the equivalent on a Shiny app object.

Examples

if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{
call_tree_dir("R", root = "launch_app")
call_tree_dir("R", root = "launch_app", modules_only = TRUE)
call_tree_dir("R", root = "launch_app", exclude = "logr_msg")
call_tree_dir("R", root = "nav_ui", keep = "^mod_counts_")
call_tree_dir("R", root = "launch_app", include_ns = "shiny", max_depth = 2)
} # }
